facts.value: Various activities initiated by students have taken place in the past. The first point of contact for meeting other students of Scandinavian Studies is the Scandinavian Studies department group, which meets regularly in the student council room (V1, ground floor, R. 157).
The student council room is open to all students when a member of the department group is present. It can be used for discussions, studying, and group work, but it is not exclusively a workroom.
The information meeting is normally held once a semester.

At the beginning of each winter semester, an orientation event for new students is held, followed by a campus tour, a possible joint lunch in the cafeteria, and a coffee reception in the student council room.
The Scandinavian Studies department group coordinates regular student activities and events at the institute, which are open to all who want to engage.
Regular bar nights and game days are organized, and details are communicated via the mailing list, announcements, and social media.
A midsummer festival takes place at the end of each summer semester, often outdoors if the weather is nice.
The Glögg festival is a cozy Christmas celebration with homemade Glögg and punch held in front of the institute's rooms, with the date announced in advance during the winter semester.
